sentence: Your skin is still healing after it looks healed.
claim: Wound remodeling continues for months to years after the surface has closed.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Remodeling runs from about day 21 and can last a year or more; one source says years. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: When a small gap in your skin closes, it looks finished in a week or two, but it isn't.
claim: Surface closure typically takes days to a couple of weeks; deeper repair continues.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Timing depends on the injury: film says 'a small gap'. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Underneath, the work has already begun.
claim: Repair starts in the first days (hemostasis, inflammation).
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Plain-language. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: First, your body seals it and calls in its cleaning crews.
claim: Hemostasis (a clot seals the injury) then inflammatory cells (neutrophils, macrophages) clear debris.
source_title: JoVE: phases of wound repair (via search)
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Phases: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, remodeling. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: New cells creep in from the edges, and repair cells lay down fresh collagen.
claim: Keratinocytes migrate from the wound edges (re-epithelialization); fibroblasts deposit collagen.
source_title: JoVE: phases of wound repair (via search)
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Proliferation phase. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Quickly, a little messily, like scaffolding.
claim: The first collagen (mostly type III) is laid down quickly and disorganized.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] 'Messy' is a plain-language word for disorganized fibres. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: But for months, sometimes a year or more, the skin keeps quietly rebuilding.
claim: Collagen production and breakdown continue for 6 months to a year or more.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Sources: 6 months to 1 year; some say years. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Then, quick collagen is traded for stronger fibers drawn slowly into line. The spot grows flatter and softer, paler.
claim: Type III collagen is replaced by type I and fibres realign along tension lines; scars flatten and fade.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Collagen switch (type I:III about 4:1 as in normal skin). 'Paler' applies to many mature scars, not all: check. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Even then, rebuilt skin usually ends up at most around eighty percent as strong as before.
claim: Healed skin regains at most about 70-80% of its original tensile strength.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Sources say about 80% (70-80%). Lay/study sources: NEEDS a primary review before posting. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: So the skin you think of as healed is still being gently rewoven, long after you've forgotten it.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Summary of c1 and c7. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.
